conventions.convention: Q_d has period 2π and probability measure (2π)^(-d) dx; Fourier coefficients use exp(-ik·x), weights are w_k=(1+|k|²)^(1/2), and real coefficient arrays satisfy a_(-k)=conjugate(a_k).

The coefficient completion is defined without Countable Choice; normalized measure, integral coefficients and L² realization assume Countable Choice. An L² realization is asserted for s≥0, not for s<0.
P_0=I; for k≠0, P_k=I-kkᵀ/|k|². QF has zero mean and coefficient -Σ_ij k_i k_j |k|^(-2) F̂_ij(k). Tensor divergence contracts the second index, so ∇QF=-(I-P)div F.

The Stokes branch assumes full AC. H₀¹ is the Sobolev-norm closure of compactly supported smooth fields; V consists of its distributionally divergence-free members. No arbitrary-domain trace characterization or solenoidal-test density equivalence is asserted.

The rectangular divergence inverse uses one linear map R with bumps fixed independently of the input and its support; each compact input-support set has a common compact output-support set, with continuity in every fixed-support test seminorm.

Rectangular distributions use real bilinear pairings and transpose derivatives with a minus sign. Pressure belongs to H⁻¹=(H₀¹)' and is determined modulo constant distributions; the pressure-class norm is the quotient norm.

Difference-energy estimates concern already given smooth solutions on the closed cylinder, with derivatives extending continuously to the endpoints. The interpolation factor is B₁(M)=1 and B_s(M)=(2M)^((s-1)/s) for s>1, including M=0.

load_bearing.statement: For d∈{1,2,3}, N≥1 and real s, H^s is the completion of finite real trigonometric polynomials in Σ_k w_k^(2s)|q̂(k)|², identified with conjugate-symmetric weighted coefficient arrays. Under Countable Choice, for s≥0 each element has a unique L² class with the specified integral coefficients.

Assume Countable Choice and d∈{1,2,3}. For integer j≥0 and σ>j+d/2, H^σ has C^j representatives with the stated norm bound. For σ>d/2, multiplication extends uniquely to a continuous bilinear map H^σ×H^σ→H^σ. These assertions extend componentwise to finite-dimensional fields.

Under Countable Choice, P and Q are real-preserving bounded multipliers on every H^s; P is an orthogonal projection. Coefficient derivatives map H^s to H^(s-1), and ∇QF=-(I-P)div F, including the zero mode.

On every nonempty finite open rectangle in dimension d≥1, a linear map R sends zero-integral scalar tests to compactly supported smooth vector tests with div(Rh)=h, common compact output support for each compact input-support set, and continuity in all fixed-support test seminorms.
Under full AC, for d≥2 and nonempty bounded open Ω⊂(-R,R)^d, the distributionally divergence-free subspace V of closure-defined H₀¹ is a real Hilbert space in the inherited H¹ pairing.
Assume full AC. For d≥2, R>0, bounded open Ω⊂(-R,R)^d and v∈H₀¹(Ω;R^d), ||v||₂≤2R||∂₁v||₂≤2R||∇v||₂.
Under full AC, on nonempty bounded open Ω⊂(-R,R)^d with d≥2, μ>0 and f∈L², there is a unique u∈V satisfying μ∫∇u:∇v=∫f·v for every v∈V, and ||∇u||₂≤2R||f||₂/μ. No pressure conclusion is asserted.
Assume Countable Choice, d∈{1,2,3}, integers m≥s≥4 and smooth real periodic f,g. For every coordinate j, ||[Λ^m,f]∂_jg||₂≤C_(d,m,s)(||f||_(H^m)||g||_(H^s)+||f||_(H^s)||g||_(H^m)).

Under Countable Choice, d∈{1,2,3}, s>d/2+1 and distributionally divergence-free u∈H^s, π=Q(u⊗u) is mean-zero and belongs to H^s, with P(u·∇u)=u·∇u+∇π in H^(s-1). It is unique among mean-zero periodic distributions satisfying this identity.

Under Countable Choice, given smooth periodic incompressible solutions with common ν≥0 satisfy the stated exponential squared-L² difference bound; given smooth solutions of the specified symmetric system with linear A_j satisfy its stated bound. A uniform rate Γ and H^s bound M yield ||w(t)||_(H^(s-1))≤B_s(M)||w(0)||₂^(1/s) exp(Γt/(2s)) for s≥1. No existence theorem is asserted.

Under full AC, on a nonempty finite open rectangle Ω⊂(-R,R)^d with d≥2, μ>0 and f∈L², the unique projected Stokes velocity admits p∈H⁻¹ satisfying -μΔu+∇p=f. Pressure is unique modulo constants and f↦(u,[p]) is bounded linear into V×(H⁻¹/R). No L² pressure or corner smoothness is asserted.

concerns.concern: Proof 3.1 says, “Smooth Fourier truncations converge in each displayed Sobolev norm,” without establishing that smooth functions belong to every weighted coefficient space. The cited definition proves cutoff convergence for elements already in H^m, while the embedding lemma gives the opposite regularity implication. The missing local justification is short: periodic integration by parts gives |f̂(k)|≤||(1-Δ)^N f||₁ w_k^(-2N), and the lattice-shell estimate then gives every required weighted summability and cutoff convergence. This is a readily closed proof gap, not a counterexample to the estimate.
